questions.question: The eponymous mongoose from Kipling’s The Jungle Book is a. Bagheera b. Baloo c. Kaa d. Rikki-Tikki-Tavi
questions.solution_html:
• The Jungle Book - forms an intertextual web – draws on traditions of Aesop’s fables
  • RKJB (Rudyard Kipling’s Jungle Book) itself is fragmented – The presence of “In the Rukh,”
  • which features an adult Mowgli, demonstrates intratextuality within Rudyard Kipling’s own
  • works. The text is also indebted to multiple pre-texts, including colonial ethnographic
  • writings like Beast and Man in India, adventure fiction such as “Nada the Lily”, and elements
  • of Hindu mythology, especially in its emphasis on law, hierarchy, and order. Thus, The Jungle
  • Book functions not merely as a single narrative but as a signifier within a larger intertextual
  • system, influencing and shaping later representations of jungle life and animal societies. In
  • this sense, it becomes a hegemonic text, capable of defining the genre it belongs to.
questions.source_exam: Reading Culture
questions.final_answer: The Jungle Book - forms an intertextual web – draws on traditions of Aesop’s fables
